MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

This is a weakly-selective neuron that fires mid-sentence in technical/software documentation and product-listing prose, peaking on a token that begins or continues a specific reference or identifier (e.g., "Sys" in SysUtils, "D" in SAMD12, the opening quote before a seller name, "to" in "pointing to", "you" in "so that you can"), while being suppressed on clause-final commas and generic nouns/pronouns like "files", "game", "there".

L10·N12633unmasked layer
This neuron fires on mid-phrase connective function words — prepositions/conjunctions like "with", "to", "and", "for", "that" — at the hinge between a role/activity phrase and its complement (e.g. "helping **with** the Assembly", "consultant **for** Luna Stage", "network partner **and** member"), rather than on any content word; the same tokens in other contexts can drive it strongly negative, so it's a position/collocation-sensitive function-word detector.
